request: a price goes from £80 to £100: what percentage increase is that?

beats.intent: A bar for £80 made of four £20 blocks
beats.narration: A ticket costs eighty pounds: four blocks of twenty.
beats.code:
stage.title("Percentage increase")
bw = 1.3
old = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=bw, height=0.7, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([-6 + 2 * bw, 1.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(old))
stage.add(old)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("£20", font_size=24).move_to(b)) for b in old])
stage.label(old, "£80", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: The new £100 price: the same four blocks plus one more £20 block in orange
beats.narration: The price rises to a hundred pounds: one more block of twenty.
beats.code:
new = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=bw, height=0.7, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)], Rectangle(width=bw, height=0.7, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([-6 + 2.5 * bw, -0.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(new))
stage.add(new)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("£20", font_size=24).move_to(b)) for b in new])
stage.label(new, "£100", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The orange block compared with the old price: 1 block out of 4, a quarter
beats.narration: Measured against the old price, the extra block is one out of four: a quarter, twenty five percent.
beats.code:
ref = SurroundingRectangle(old, color=BLUE, buff=0.06)
ext = SurroundingRectangle(new[4], color=ORANGE, buff=0.06)
stage.play(Create(ref), Create(ext))
stage.add(ref, ext)
stage.label(ext, "20 out of 80 = 25%", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The bars beside 20 ÷ 80 = 25% up, but 20 ÷ 100 = 20% back down
beats.narration: Percentage change is measured from where you start. Up from eighty is twenty five percent; back down from a hundred is only twenty percent.

request: how long is the diagonal from corner to corner inside a 3 by 4 by 12 box?

beats.intent: A tall box 4 wide, 3 deep and 12 high, drawn in perspective
beats.narration: A box is four wide, three deep and twelve tall. How long is the longest stick that fits inside, corner to corner?
beats.code:
stage.title("The diagonal of a box")
k = 0.28
o = np.array([-4.8, -2.4, 0])
W = 4 * k * RIGHT
D = 3 * k * 0.6 * np.array([1, 1, 0])
H = 12 * k * UP
P = {"f0": o, "f1": o + W, "b0": o + D, "b1": o + W + D}
P.update({key + "t": v + H for key, v in list(P.items())})
pairs = [("f0", "f1"), ("f1", "b1"), ("b1", "b0"), ("b0", "f0"), ("f0t", "f1t"), ("f1t", "b1t"), ("b1t", "b0t"), ("b0t", "f0t"), ("f0", "f0t"), ("f1", "f1t"), ("b0", "b0t"), ("b1", "b1t")]
box = VGroup(*[Line(P[a], P[b], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=2) for a, b in pairs])
stage.play(Create(box))
stage.add(box)
stage.label(Line(P["f0"], P["f1"]), "4", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(Line(P["f1"], P["b1"]), "3", direction=RIGHT)
stage.label(Line(P["f0"], P["f0t"]), "12", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: The floor diagonal from front-left to back-right corner: 5
beats.narration: First go across the floor, from one corner to the opposite one. That's the hypotenuse of a three by four right triangle: five.
beats.code:
floor_d = Line(P["f0"], P["b1"], color=GREEN, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(Create(floor_d))
stage.add(floor_d)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("5", font_size=28, color=GREEN).move_to((P["f0"] + P["b1"]) / 2 + 0.3 * DOWN + 0.15 * RIGHT)))

beats.intent: The diagonal rising from that corner to the opposite top corner, a right triangle of 5, 12 and 13 shaded
beats.narration: Now stand that floor diagonal up against the twelve tall edge: another right triangle. Its long side runs corner to corner through the box: thirteen.
beats.code:
tri = Polygon(P["f0"], P["b1"], P["b1t"], color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.25)
space_d = Line(P["f0"], P["b1t"], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(FadeIn(tri), Create(space_d))
stage.add(tri, space_d)
stage.label(space_d, "13", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.narration: Pythagoras twice: three, four, five across the floor, then five, twelve, thirteen up through the box.

request: why are vertically opposite angles equal?

beats.intent: Two straight lines crossing at a point
beats.code:
stage.title("Vertically opposite angles")
O = np.array([-3, -0.3, 0])
d = np.array([np.cos(50 * DEGREES), np.sin(50 * DEGREES), 0])
l1 = Line(O + 3 * LEFT, O + 3 * RIGHT, color=WHITE)
l2 = Line(O - 2.8 * d, O + 2.8 * d, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(l1), Create(l2))
stage.add(l1, l2)

beats.intent: Angle a = 50° and its neighbour b = 130° marked: together they make a straight line
beats.narration: Mark an angle a, fifty degrees, and the angle b next to it. Together they make a straight line, so b is a hundred and thirty.
beats.code:
a = Angle(Line(O, O + RIGHT), Line(O, O + d), radius=0.7, color=YELLOW)
b = Angle(Line(O, O + d), Line(O, O + LEFT), radius=0.5, color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(a), Create(b))
stage.add(a, b)
stage.label(a, "a = 50°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(b, "b = 130°", direction=UP, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Angle c, opposite a, marked 50°: b and c also make a straight line
beats.narration: The angle c, opposite a, also sits next to b on a straight line. So c is a hundred and eighty minus a hundred and thirty: fifty, the same as a.
beats.code:
c = Angle(Line(O, O + LEFT), Line(O, O - d), radius=0.7, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(c))
stage.add(c)
stage.label(c, "c = 50°", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The lines beside a + b = 180°, b + c = 180°, so a = c
beats.narration: Both a and c are what's left when b is taken from a straight line, so vertically opposite angles are always equal.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"a + b = 180^\circ", r"b + c = 180^\circ", r"a = c")

request: how does the cosine rule find a missing side?

beats.intent: A triangle with sides 5 and 7 meeting at a 60° angle
beats.narration: A triangle has sides five and seven, with a sixty degree angle between them.
beats.code:
stage.title("The cosine rule")
k = 0.55
A = np.array([-5.6, -2.0, 0])
B = A + 7 * k * RIGHT
C = A + 5 * k * np.array([np.cos(PI / 3), np.sin(PI / 3), 0])
sides = VGroup(Line(A, B, color=WHITE), Line(A, C, color=WHITE))
stage.play(Create(sides))
stage.add(sides)
ang = Angle(Line(A, B), Line(A, C), radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(ang))
stage.add(ang)
stage.label(ang, "60°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(sides[0], "7", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(sides[1], "5", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: The third side a drawn in orange with a question mark
beats.narration: The third side, opposite the angle, is unknown. Call it a.
beats.code:
a_side = Line(B, C, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(Create(a_side))
stage.add(a_side)
m = (B + C) / 2
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("a = ?", font_size=28, color=ORANGE).move_to(m + 0.5 * (m - A) / np.linalg.norm(m - A))))

beats.intent: A faint right-angled version with the 5 side standing straight up: its third side √74 ≈ 8.6 is longer
beats.narration: If the angle were ninety degrees, Pythagoras would give a squared equals twenty five plus forty nine, seventy four. A narrower angle pulls the sides together, so the real a is shorter: the cosine rule subtracts the difference.
beats.code:
C2 = A + 5 * k * UP
ghost = VGroup(DashedLine(A, C2, color=GREY_B), DashedLine(B, C2, color=GREY_B))
stage.play(Create(ghost))
stage.add(ghost)
stage.label(ghost[1], "at 90°: √74 ≈ 8.6", direction=UP, color=GREY_B)

beats.narration: a squared is twenty five plus forty nine minus two times five times seven times a half: thirty nine. So a is about six point two four.
